title: Generative Flows on Discrete State-Spaces: Enabling Multimodal Flows with Applications to Protein Co-Design

nodes.text: Discrete Flow Models (DFMs) are a flow-based generative model for discrete data in which the discrete equivalent of continuous-space flow matching is realized using Continuous Time Markov Chains (CTMCs).
nodes.evidence: the discrete equivalent of continuous space flow matching can be realized using Continuous Time Markov Chains.

nodes.text: DFMs include discrete diffusion models as a specific instance while allowing improved performance over existing diffusion-based approaches.
nodes.evidence: DFMs benefit from a simple derivation that includes discrete diffusion models as a specific instance while allowing improved performance over existing diffusion-based approaches.

nodes.text: DFMs provide the missing link enabling flow-based generative models to be applied to multimodal continuous-and-discrete data problems.
nodes.evidence: a new flow-based model of discrete data that provides the missing link in enabling flow-based generative models to be applied to multimodal continuous and discrete data problems.

nodes.text: Flow-based models improve over diffusion models by allowing sampling flexibility without retraining, whereas diffusion models' sample-time inflexibility makes them unsuitable for multimodal problems where optimal sampling parameters require extensive retraining.
nodes.evidence: their sample time inflexibility makes them unsuitable for multimodal problems ... flow-based models ... improve over diffusion models with a simpler framework that allows for superior performance through sampling flexibility

nodes.text: A neural network is trained with cross-entropy to predict the clean datapoint x1 from noisy data xt, and the choice of rate matrix Rt is deferred until after training, enabling inference-time sampling flexibility.
nodes.evidence: Lce does not depend on Rt(xt, j|x1) and so we can postpone the choice of Rt(xt, j|x1) until after training. This enables inference time flexibility

nodes.text: CTMC stochasticity, controlled by a parameter eta that adds a detailed-balance rate matrix to a base rate matrix, adjusts the number of state transitions in a trajectory at inference without retraining.
nodes.evidence: We refer to the behaviour that eta controls as CTMC stochasticity.

nodes.text: Prior discrete diffusion models are equivalent to picking a specific CTMC stochasticity at training time, whereas DFMs can adjust it at inference to enhance sample quality and control distributional properties.
nodes.evidence: Prior discrete diffusion models are equivalent to picking a specific stochasticity at training time, whereas we can adjust it at inference: enhancing sample quality and exerting control over sample distributional properties.

nodes.text: Multiflow is a multimodal generative model for protein co-design that combines a DFM for discrete sequence generation with a continuous flow-based structure generation method, jointly generating structure and sequence while conditioning on either modality.
nodes.evidence: developing a novel continuous structure and discrete sequence generative model named Multiflow.

nodes.text: Unlike previous multimodal approaches that generated only sequence or only structure and used a separate prediction model for the other, a single Multiflow model jointly generates sequence and structure and conditions on either.
nodes.evidence: Previous multimodal approaches either generated only the sequence or only the structure and then used a prediction model to infer the remaining modality ... Our single model can jointly generate sequence and structure

nodes.text: On small-scale text data, DFMs outperform the discrete diffusion alternative D3PM through their expanded sample-time flexibility.
nodes.evidence: DFMs outperform the discrete diffusion alternative, D3PM (Austin et al., 2021) through their expanded sample time flexibility.

nodes.text: Multiflow achieves state-of-the-art protein co-design performance, and with data distillation also achieves state-of-the-art structure generation.
nodes.evidence: Multiflow achieves state-of-the-art co-design performance while data distillation allows for obtaining state-of-the-art structure generation.

nodes.text: CTMC stochasticity enables controlling sample properties such as secondary structure composition and diversity in generated proteins.
nodes.evidence: We find CTMC stochasticity enables controlling sample properties such as secondary structure composition and diversity.

nodes.text: The construction of the generative probability flow from conditional flows via a rate matrix is analogous to building generative probability paths from conditional paths in continuous flow matching (Lipman et al., 2023), with a rate matrix replacing the continuous vector field.
nodes.evidence: analogous to the construction of generative probability paths from conditional probability paths in Lipman et al. (2023), where instead of a continuous vector field generating the probability path, we have a rate matrix generating the probability flow.

nodes.text: Setting eta=0 (using the base rate matrix Rt*) minimizes the expected number of jumps during the sequence trajectory because the ReLU removes state pairs that needlessly exchange mass.
nodes.evidence: Rt* generates pt|1 whilst minimizing the expected number of jumps during the sequence trajectory.
